participation.context: Kept the custom at one bough, and ended the porch.
participation.name: Mistress Dorcas Ansell

participation.context: Said she had not brought a second bough.
participation.name: Alse Pinder

participation.context: Left the bough unimproved, and saved the book for the stair.
participation.name: William Shakespeare

relations.note: she allows one bough and no woodland

story.body: Mistress Ansell named the single hawthorn bough and refused a second. You said it was drooping. Nobody counted the heads. You took the lump in the cloak back to the stair.

relations.note: she allows one bough and no woodland

title: Left the one bough as it was

participation.context: Named the oath, kept the three pence, and named the sixpence and the quarter.
participation.name: Mistress Dorcas Ansell

participation.context: Saw the lump and the ink, and was told to shut the chronicle.
participation.name: Alse Pinder

participation.context: Took the comedy, refused the chronicle, and went.
participation.name: William Shakespeare

relations.note: the chronicle stays out, and the comedy is the book that can be left

story.body: You put the comedy under your cloak and left the chronicle upstairs. Mistress Ansell kept her three pence and the sleeping sixpence, and sent you over the cat. You called Thursday's forty lines a part.

relations.note: the chronicle stays out, and the comedy is the book that can be left
